models.name: resnet50
limitations: Trained on ImageNet-1k: only recognises those 1000 categories, and will confidently return a wrong label for anything outside them.
ImageNet is known to under-represent non-Western contexts, so accuracy is uneven across geographies and cultures.
Expects a single dominant subject; cluttered scenes with several objects are better served by the detection endpoint.
Confidence is not calibrated — a 0.9 score does not mean 90% correct.
models.description: resnet50 pretrained on ImageNet-1k, exported to ONNX. Serves general-purpose image classification over 1000 categories.

models.name: resnet50-embed
limitations: Features come from an ImageNet classifier, so they encode 'what object is this' far better than style, colour or composition.
Not trained with a contrastive objective, so it is weaker at instance-level retrieval (finding the same specific object) than a purpose-built model such as CLIP or DINOv2.
Similarity scores are only comparable within one index built by one model version; re-embedding is required after a model change.
Search is exact brute force, which is linear in index size. Beyond ~1M vectors, switch to an approximate index.
models.description: resnet50 backbone with the classification head removed, emitting 2048-dimensional L2-normalised embeddings for similarity search.

models.name: yolov8n
limitations: Trained on COCO's 80 categories only; anything else is either missed entirely or mislabelled as the nearest COCO class.
The nano variant trades accuracy for speed. Small, distant or heavily occluded objects are frequently missed.
Fixed 640x640 input: very wide or very tall images lose detail after letterboxing, which hurts recall on small objects.
Crowded scenes suffer from non-maximum suppression merging genuinely separate, overlapping objects into one box.
models.description: yolov8n (YOLOv8 nano) trained on COCO, exported to ONNX. Detects 80 common object categories with bounding boxes.
